intro: We use “should” to give advice or a recommendation, and to say what is right or a good idea to do. It is an essential tool to help someone, give your opinion or ask for advice.
objectifs: Form should / shouldn't + base verb and the question Should I…?
Give advice naturally with I think you should / I don't think you should.
Ask for advice (What should I do?).
Tell the difference between should (advice) and must / have to (obligation).

texte: “Should” is a modal verb, like must and will: it never changes (no -s) and it is followed by the base verb without to.
Negative: should not, short form “shouldn't”. Question: put should before the subject. Short answers: Yes, you should. / No, you shouldn't.

lignes: Yes, you should. / No, you shouldn't.
Should I go? — Yes, you should.

texte: “You should + base” is the simplest way to give advice. To be more polite or less direct, add “I think” or “maybe”: “I think you should…”, “Maybe you should…”.
For negative advice, English prefers “I don't think you should…” to “I think you shouldn't…”, as with will (lesson 49).
exemples: You look tired. You should go to bed early.
Simple advice.
I think you should talk to your manager.
Softer advice.
I don't think you should buy that car. It's too old.
Negative advice: I don't think + should.
Maybe we should take a taxi.
A gentle suggestion.

texte: To ask for someone's opinion, use “Should I…?” or “What / Where / When should I…?”. You can also ask “What do you think I should do?”.
Be careful: in “What do you think I should do?”, the word order after “do you think” is like a statement: I should do, not “should I do”.
exemples: Should I bring something to the party?
Yes / no question.
Which course should I choose?
Wh- question.
What do you think I should do?
Statement order after do you think.

texte: “Should” is advice: you can choose. “Must” and “have to” are obligation (lesson 54). Compare: “You should wear a coat” (it's a good idea, it's cold) and “You must wear a helmet” (it's the rule).
“Ought to” means almost the same as should, but it is less common and a bit more formal: “You ought to apologise”. “You'd better + base” is stronger: if you don't do it, there will be a problem.

lignes: You ought to see a doctor.
strong advice, or there's a problem
You'd better see a doctor before it gets worse.
You must / have to see a doctor to get a certificate.

sections.titre: Should for what is right or expected
texte: “Should” also expresses what is right or correct: a moral opinion or a criticism. It can also show a logical expectation: what will probably happen if everything is normal.
The fixed phrase “If I were you, I'd…” is another very common way to give advice; you will study its grammar at B1.
exemples: People shouldn't throw rubbish in the street.
Opinion: it's wrong.
The bus should arrive in five minutes.
Expectation: it will probably arrive.
If I were you, I'd accept the offer.
Advice with a fixed phrase.

formule: should / shouldn't + base verb · Should I + base …? · I (don't) think you should + base
prononciation: “should” is /ʃʊd/: the l is silent, and the vowel is short as in “book”. Weak form: /ʃəd/.
“shouldn't” is /ˈʃʊdnt/: two syllables, a light t.
“could”, “would” and “should” all rhyme: /kʊd/, /wʊd/, /ʃʊd/ (the l is never pronounced).
To make advice softer, the voice goes down and then up a little: “Maybe you should ↘ call her ↗”.
erreurs: I don't think you should go.
More natural: put the negative on think.
What do you think should I do?
What do you think I should do?
After “do you think”, use statement order.
You must try to relax a bit.
You should try to relax a bit.
Just advice, not an obligation: should.
I should went to the doctor.
I should go to the doctor.

dialogue.contexte: Inès, a student in Brussels, can't sleep before her exams. She talks to her friend Mariam.
lignes: I can't sleep at all. My exams start next week. What should I do?
First, you shouldn't drink coffee after four o'clock.
Oh. I drink three cups in the evening!
That's too much. And I think you should turn off your phone an hour before bed.
Should I study at night when it's quiet?
No, I don't think you should. Your brain needs rest. Study in the morning.
OK. Maybe I should go for a walk every day too.
Maybe I should = a gentle idea.
Great idea! And if you still can't sleep, you should see a doctor.

mots: Can I give you some advice?
an opinion about what someone should do (uncountable)
The doctor advised me to rest.
to tell someone what you think they should do
to give an idea for someone to think about
to relax, sleep or stop working; a time of relaxing
good for your body; not ill
He's under a lot of stress.
a feeling of worry because of problems or work
I have a problem with my landlord.
In my opinion, you should accept.

items: You have a fever. You ___ go to work today.
It's very cold. You ___ wear a warm jacket.
You ___ eat so much sugar. It's bad for your teeth.
We ___ leave now, or we'll miss the train.

exercices.consigne: Give advice with You should / You shouldn't.
items: You should take an aspirin and rest. / You shouldn't look at your screen.
I always arrive late at work.
You should practise every day and watch films in English.
You shouldn't buy things you don't need.
what / we / buy / for Ali's birthday?
What should we buy for Ali's birthday?
Where should I stay in Montreal?

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
items: You should to drink more water.
Do we should book a table?
I don't think you should worry.

exercices.consigne: Rewrite the sentence with should, shouldn't or What … should …?
items: It's a good idea for you to call your sister.
It isn't a good idea for us to come home too late.
We shouldn't come home too late.
Tell me your opinion: what is the right thing for me to do?
What do you think I should do?

exercices.consigne: A friend is visiting your town for the first time. Give five pieces of advice (at least one negative and one with I don't think you should).
items: Welcome to Douala! You should try the grilled fish at Youpwe. You should always agree on the price before you take a moto-taxi. You shouldn't walk alone late at night in quiet areas. I don't think you should rent a car — the traffic is crazy! And you should visit the Doual'art gallery.

a_retenir: Questions: Should I…? / What should I do? (no do).
More polite: I think you should… / Maybe you should…; negative: I don't think you should…
should = advice (a choice); must / have to = obligation.
“should” is pronounced /ʃʊd/: the l is silent.
